name: Pashur the son of Immer
charge: Smiting the prophet of the Lord and putting him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin; prophesying lies
summary: Pashur the son of Immer, priest and chief governor in the house of the Lord, struck Jeremiah and put him in the stocks at the high gate of Benjamin after Jeremiah prophesied the breaking of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 19:14-15; Jeremiah 20:1-2). The next day Jeremiah renamed him Magor-missabib, fear round about, and told him he would see his friends fall, and would go to Babylon, die and be buried there with the friends to whom he had prophesied lies (Jeremiah 20:3-6).
offenseFull: Jeremiah had come from Tophet, where he broke the potter’s vessel before the elders as a sign that the Lord would break the people and the city beyond repair, and then stood in the court of the Lord’s house and told all the people the evil was coming because they had hardened their necks and would not hear (Jeremiah 19:10-15). The class that reads chapter 19 straight into chapter 20 draws the lesson: rather than hear what the Bible says, they hit, hurt and stopped the one who said it. Pashur the son of Immer, the priest who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard it, struck Jeremiah, and put him in the stocks in the high gate of Benjamin by the house of the Lord (Jeremiah 20:1-2). The teacher marks this as the place where the opposition to Jeremiah starts.

The class explains the words: smote means he struck him, flogged him, and the stocks were public shaming, meant to break a man’s spirit. Another class set pictures of the slave stocks beside this verse: we have lived the same atrocities our forefathers went through. Pashur did it because he was tired of Jeremiah blasting them for their wickedness and corruption, and Judah was worse than the northern kingdom because they knew better. The teaching keeps him apart from Pashur the son of Malchiah, who later sought Jeremiah’s death (Jeremiah 21:1; Jeremiah 38:1); this Pashur was the priest showing that he had power and a position.

He was also a false prophet. Jeremiah’s sentence names the friends to whom he had prophesied lies (Jeremiah 20:6), and the Luke 20 teaching sets him beside the husbandmen who beat the servants sent to them (Luke 20:10-11), giving his stance as the priest who says God is not talking to you, I am the priest. Jeremiah 23 describes the same house: prophet and priest both profane, wickedness found even in the Lord’s house, and prophets speaking a vision of their own heart and not from the mouth of the Lord (Jeremiah 23:11; Jeremiah 23:16). The study note compares the pastor who says, let me tell you what God told me to tell you, when it is a lie. The class of 2026-07-18 draws the application from Pashur’s stocks: prophecy is not all loves and kisses; we are supposed to prophesy destruction so our people may wake up, and destruction is headed to America.
judgmentFull: The next day Pashur let him out, and Jeremiah told him the Lord had not called his name Pashur but Magor-missabib, which the class explains just means fear round about: he would be a terror to himself and to all his friends, and would watch them fall by the sword of their enemies (Jeremiah 20:3-4). All Judah would be given to the king of Babylon, with the strength of the city, its labours, its precious things and the treasures of the kings of Judah; the teacher notes that this shows our people had treasures, their own land and wealth (Jeremiah 20:4-5). Pashur and everyone in his house would go into captivity, and he would die in Babylon and be buried there with the friends to whom he had prophesied lies (Jeremiah 20:6).

The stocks did not break Jeremiah’s spirit, the class says; he was emboldened by it. Jeremiah had no power of his own to give Judah to Babylon; it was the spirit of the Lord speaking. As the Luke 20 teaching puts it, do what you want to the messenger, it will not stop the judgment. When the city fell, the nobles of Judah were slain at Riblah before Zedekiah’s eyes, and the teacher turns back from that verse to the word spoken to Pashur, that his own eyes would see people he would not expect put to death (Jeremiah 39:6; Jeremiah 20:4). The chapter records the sentence and not its carrying out; the captivity that the priest’s lies denied came as Jeremiah said.

lawsResolved.text: God will punish civil authorities who punish unjustly and contrary to the law.
Lying pastors and those that withhold the truth of God's word are cursed for causing national apostasy.
Scourging or whipping (not to exceed forty stripes).
Priests are to keep God's law and statutes in all of his assemblies.

text.text: Then came Jeremiah from Tophet, whither the Lord had sent him to prophesy; and he stood in the court of the Lord’s house; and said to all the people,

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon this city and upon all her towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it, because they have hardened their necks, that they might not hear my words.
Now Pashur the son of Immer the priest, who was also chief governor in the house of the Lord, heard that Jeremiah prophesied these things.
Then Pashur smote Jeremiah the prophet, and put him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Benjamin, which was by the house of the Lord.
And it came to pass on the morrow, that Pashur brought forth Jeremiah out of the stocks. Then said Jeremiah unto him, The Lord hath not called thy name Pashur, but Magor–missabib.

For thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will make thee a terror to thyself, and to all thy friends: and they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and thine eyes shall behold it: and I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall carry them captive into Babylon, and shall slay them with the sword.

Moreover I will deliver all the strength of this city, and all the labours thereof, and all the precious things thereof, and all the treasures of the kings of Judah will I give into the hand of their enemies, which shall spoil them, and take them, and carry them to Babylon.

And thou, Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house shall go into captivity: and thou shalt come to Babylon, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buried there, thou, and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.
Then shalt thou break the bottle in the sight of the men that go with thee,

And shalt say unto them, Thus saith the Lord of hosts; Even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaketh a potter’s vessel, that cannot be made whole again: and they shall bury them in Tophet, till there be no place to bury.
Thus will I do unto this place, saith the Lord, and to the inhabitants thereof, and even make this city as Tophet:

And the houses of Jerusalem, and the houses of the kings of Judah, shall be defiled as the place of Tophet, because of all the houses upon whose roofs they have burned incense unto all the host of heaven, and have poured out drink offerings unto other gods.
Then came Jeremiah from Tophet, whither the Lord had sent him to prophesy; and he stood in the court of the Lord’s house; and said to all the people,

Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel; Behold, I will bring upon this city and upon all her towns all the evil that I have pronounced against it, because they have hardened their necks, that they might not hear my words.
The word which came unto Jeremiah from the Lord, when king Zedekiah sent unto him Pashur the son of Melchiah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, saying,

Then Shephatiah the son of Mattan, and Gedaliah the son of Pashur, and Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashur the son of Malchiah, heard the words that Jeremiah had spoken unto all the people, saying,

And thou, Pashur, and all that dwell in thine house shall go into captivity: and thou shalt come to Babylon, and there thou shalt die, and shalt be buried there, thou, and all thy friends, to whom thou hast prophesied lies.
And at the season he sent a servant to the husbandmen, that they should give him of the fruit of the vineyard: but the husbandmen beat him, and sent him away empty.
And again he sent another servant: and they beat him also, and entreated him shamefully, and sent him away empty.
For both prophet and priest are profane; yea, in my house have I found their wickedness, saith the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord of hosts, Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.

Now it came to pass, when Jeremiah had made an end of speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to speak unto all the people, that the priests and the prophets and all the people took him, saying, Thou shalt surely die.

Why hast thou prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying, This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate without an inhabitant? And all the people were gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
When the princes of Judah heard these things, then they came up from the king’s house unto the house of the Lord, and sat down in the entry of the new gate of the Lord’s house.
Then spake the priests and the prophets unto the princes and to all the people, saying, This man is worthy to die; for he hath prophesied against this city, as ye have heard with your ears.
